items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5839

SPONSOR: KAVANAGH
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the election law, in relation to the
form of primary election ballots; to amend a chapter of the laws of
2019, amending the election law relating to enacting the voter friendly
ballot act, as proposed in legislative bills numbers S.  2300-A and A.
2682-A, in relation to the effectiveness thereof; and repealing certain
provisions of such law relating thereto

 
PURPOSE:

To ensure counties can purchase and use cost effective election equip-
ment while maintaining ballot integrity.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill repeals subdivision 2(h) of § 7-114 of the
election law.

Section 2 of this bill repeals Paragraph (c) of subdivision 2 of § 7-114
of the election law, as amended by a chapter of the laws of 2019, amend-
ing the election law relating to enacting the voter friendly ballot act,
as proposed in legislative bills numbers S. 2300-A and A. 2682-A.

Section 3 of this bill amends subdivision 1 of § 16-104 of the election
law to remove the reference to color coding of the primary ballot.

Section 4 amends Section 17 of a chapter of the laws of 2019, relating
to enacting the voter friendly ballot act, as proposed in legislative
bills numbers S. 2300-A and A. 2682-A, to change the effective date to
July 1, 2020

Section 5 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Election Law imposes the need for political parties to be assigned a
color on their respective primary election ballots. With the advent of
early voting, subsequent use of electronic poll books, and ballot on
demand (BOD) printers, the need for color coding has been rendered obso-
lete. The color designation is largely a hold-over from the use of lever
machines, when poll workers were handed a colored piece of paper so they
could manually change to the appropriate ballot, then on pre-printed
paper ballots as a way to presumably prevent poll worker error.

Until now, there has not been a considerable cost differential to comply
with the color coding requirements. However, with the new requirement of
counties to purchase new voting equipment such as ballot on demand prin-
ters, maintaining the status-quo will cost counties millions of dollars
more to provide color notations for ballots.  With electronic poll books
and BOD printers, voters will automatically receive the appropriate
ballot and the color bar is effectively unnecessary.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Reduction in equipment costs to country board of elections.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately; provided, however, that sections
one and three of this act shall take effect January 1, 2020; provided
further that section two of this act shall take effect on the same date
and in the same manner as a chapter of the laws of 2019, amending the
election law relating to enacting the voter friendly ballot act, as
proposed in legislative bills numbers S.  2300-A and A. 2682-A, takes
effect.

summary: Relates to the form of primary ballots; removes color requirement.
